title: Where art thou (Genesis 3:8–13)
hookLine: God walks in the garden in the cool of the day and calls for the hiding couple

cards: A kid breaks a vase. The parent hears the crash from the kitchen, walks into the living room, and the room is empty. Except for two small feet sticking out from behind the curtain.
Everyone knows exactly where the child is. And still the parent says, out loud, gently or not: where are you? That's Genesis today.
The fruit is eaten, the fig leaves are sewn, and the evening breeze comes through the garden, and with it, the sound of someone walking.

teach.b: First, the walk. Genesis says the man and the woman heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the garden, in the afternoon air, the cool of the day.
It's an astonishingly close picture of God: not thunder, but footsteps at evening, as if this were a habit. And they hide among the trees. Then the question.
In the Douay-Rheims: "And the Lord God called Adam, and said to him: Where art thou?"
In Hebrew it's one word, ayekkah. God made the man from dust; God isn't asking for directions.
Teachers in both Jewish and Christian tradition have read it this way: the question is for Adam, a chance to come out on his own.
His answer is painfully honest: "I heard thy voice in paradise; and I was afraid, because I was naked, and I hid myself." Afraid, naked, hid. No excuses yet.
Then the blame. God asks who told him he was naked, and whether he ate. The man points: the woman you gave me, she gave me the fruit.
He blames her and, quietly, God too. The woman points at the serpent.
The Catechism says the harmony of the garden is broken here: between the man and woman, with creation, and with God. And yet God's first word to the man who has hidden is not a sentence.
It's a question that goes looking for him. Catholics hear the same call in confession: come out from behind the trees and say it.

how: In the sacrament of reconciliation, Catholics name their own sins aloud to a priest, rather than explaining others' faults, and receive absolution.

games.q: you're Adam, crouched among the trees. you hear footsteps, and a voice calls: where art thou? what do you do?
o: answer: I heard thy voice, I was afraid, and I hid.
games.why: he answers, honestly at first: afraid, naked, hid. then, asked what he did, he blames the woman God gave him.

practice: Ask yourself the old question slowly: where are you hiding?

Maybe behind being busy, behind a joke, behind a story where it was mostly someone else's fault; pick one tree, and picture taking one step out from it into the evening air, where someone is calling your name.
If you pray, you can answer with Adam's honest words: I was afraid.

wordCard.voice: Ayekkah, God's one-word question to a man hiding in the trees: not for information, but an invitation to come out. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: where are you? one word, God's question to Adam hiding in the garden.

carryVoice: Your line: afraid, naked, hid. Three honest words, said before any excuse. See you tomorrow.
